speaker: Doctor
text: That's a good start. Can you describe exactly how your walking has changed, and do you experience any numbness, weakness, or vision changes? Also, have you noticed any involuntary movements or tremors?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the "drunk" appearance and right-sided clumsiness are concerning. Do you have a history of back pain, spinal trauma, or any recent infections like meningitis? Additionally, have you ever been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis or any other neurological condition?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to natalizumab therapy. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_with_contrast. REQUEST TEST: JC_virus_antibody_status.

Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, this combination of ataxia and clumsy gait is highly suggestive of PML. Please wait for the MRI results while I arrange for the JC virus testing.
